title: Entrance checkpoint: oblique view from inside the same hall
prompt: Create ONE wide photorealistic human-eye-height architectural image, a supplemental camera view of the exact same hall in the two supplied images. Reference image 1, 02-EntranceSecurity.png, is the PRIMARY scene and controls the entrance architecture and checkpoint placement and massing. Reference image 2, 01-InnerEnd.png, is the opposite view of this SAME hall, supplied only for consistency of columns, materials, floor and side aisles; its small opaque inner-end door belongs at the opposite end and must not be transplanted to the entrance. Move the camera closer to the entrance checkpoint while remaining inside the hall, offset toward the left side of the central approach as seen in reference image 1, looking diagonally toward the glazed entrance. Use a natural wide rectilinear perspective at standing eye level, with straight verticals and no fisheye. Frame the checkpoint clearly in the middle distance and include the adjacent left column bay and its existing side aisle, with enough visible continuous floor to read how the hall-side checkpoint area meets that aisle. Keep the equipment in its existing location: the single slender dark metal-detector frame is to the right of the compact low security desk/screening equipment when facing the entrance, as in image 1. Reveal their depth and separation through the camera angle, retaining their sparse dark metal forms and modest footprint; interpret obscured equipment details minimally. Do not enlarge this into an airport screening installation or add security stations. Preserve the massive square dark green-grey veined stone columns, horizontal panel seams, repeated column rhythm, heavy stone lintels, higher central space, narrower flanking aisles, polished green-grey veined floor and its two parallel black strips continuing toward the entrance. Preserve the tall mullioned glazed entrance end above the glazed entry, cool linear side-aisle lights, subdued daylight, austere institutional mood and readable stone and metal reflections. Keep the architecture and the checkpoint legible with restrained contrast; do not hide details in darkness or fog. Maintain the room's reference proportions and arrangement, changing only viewpoint rather than redesigning it. No new side doors, invented off-camera corridors, turnstile arrays, plants, art, ornament, decorative ceiling coffers, three-elevator wall, damage, debris, people, bodies, narrative events or spatial anomalies. Do not use the superseded Review01-A/B/C concepts or rejected prototype dimensions. Output one coherent landscape image only, without labels, captions, diagrams, inset panels, collage or extra variants.
